classification.difficultyReason: Identify the red–red and blue–blue paths, update the matching-colour probability after each possible first draw without replacement, and add the two path products.

content.prompt: A box contains 7 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are chosen randomly. What is the probability of both balls being the same colour if

children.label: a
children.prompt: the balls were chosen with replacement.

answer.worked:
With replacement, the second draw has the same colour probabilities as the first.

$$\begin{align*} P(\text{same colour}) &= P(\text{both red})+P(\text{both blue}) \\ P(\text{same colour}) &= \frac{7}{10}\times\frac{7}{10}+\frac{3}{10}\times\frac{3}{10} \\ P(\text{same colour}) &= \frac{29}{50} \end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the balls were chosen without replacement.

answer.worked:
On the second draw, 9 balls remain, including 6 red if the first ball was red or 2 blue if it was blue.

$$\begin{align*} P(\text{same colour}) &= P(\text{both red})+P(\text{both blue}) \\ P(\text{same colour}) &= \frac{7}{10}\times\frac{6}{9}+\frac{3}{10}\times\frac{2}{9} \\ P(\text{same colour}) &= \frac{8}{15} \end{align*}$$
